correctness.rationale: For a prescribed permutation cell the degree is exactly a+b-2K with hypergeometric K. Uniform sampling-without-replacement concentration localizes every fixed-threshold extreme to O(sqrt(n)) diagonal/anti-diagonal corners. Inside those corners the discrepancy between degree and corner score is uniformly O_P(1), bounded by a tight corner-cell count. Four-corner mixed factorial moments prove independent unit Poisson fields; an almost-sure continuous graph map recovers every induced edge. Explicit triangle integration and independent Poisson pair means give t^4/6 vs t^4/3. Standalone exhaustive checker confirms finite identities but not the limit.

originality.rationale: The full 2015 preprint and author-hosted revised article give marginal extremal-degree information (not a four-corner marked induced-graph limit), and the directly relevant published two-corner Poisson result describes only anti-diagonal corners and global inversions. The new conclusion is a four-way simultaneously coupled marked point-process and its full inversion-induced edge structure; in particular two vertex classes with the same Poisson count distribution have distinct nontrivial expected internal edge counts. These comparisons are about claim implication, not title matching. An earlier general marked-permutation-extrema theorem is a specific unresolved priority risk.

value.rationale: Extremal vertex *sets and their mutual graph structure* are natural global/local invariants of a random permutation graph. The theorem supplies a complete limiting finite random graph with spatially marked low/high vertices, ordered degree thresholds, and contrasting induced edge intensities t^4/6 versus t^4/3, which cannot be inferred from the classical marginal Rayleigh law. The induced adjacency structure captures real dependence rather than a renamed scalar asymptotic and enables exact limiting calculations for multiple extremes.
